# Computer Use

You operate apps on the user's macOS or Windows computer with agent-desktop
1.1.0. The guide below is agent-desktop's own; then read the one for the
host's OS: `/opt/gamut/docs/computer-use/macos.md` or `/opt/gamut/docs/computer-use/windows.md`.

## How you run it here

- **Tools are the commands**, the `mcp__agent-desktop__` tools.
  `computer_<command>` runs `agent-desktop <command>`: its params are the
  command's arguments (`<REF>` is `ref`) and flags (`--wait-for` is
  `wait_for`). They are `computer_list_apps`, `computer_list_windows`, `computer_snapshot`, `computer_find`, `computer_get`, `computer_is`, `computer_screenshot`, `computer_list_surfaces`, `computer_click`, `computer_double_click`, `computer_right_click`, `computer_type`, `computer_set_value`, `computer_select`, `computer_scroll`, `computer_press`, `computer_hover`, `computer_mouse_click`, `computer_wait`, `computer_launch`, `computer_close_app`.
  `mcp__agent-desktop__agent_desktop({ args })` runs any command, as its
  argument list without `agent-desktop`, the command first (e.g.
  `["drag", "--from", "@s1:e2", "--to", "@s1:e5", "--headed"]`). There is no
  shell, so pass each argument as its own string. Every command's flags:
  `/opt/gamut/docs/computer-use/flags.md`.
- **Results** are what agent-desktop prints. A screenshot comes back as an
  image, with a line saying which screen points it shows.
- **One call at a time.** Calls sent together run one after another, each as
  soon as the one before returns, even when an earlier one failed or has not
  taken effect: send a step that depends on another only after reading its
  result. An action can return before the app has reacted to it (a menu
  opening, focus moving, a page loading), so a screenshot or another action
  sent with it can see the screen from before it. Check what an action did in
  your next turn, or wait for the change: `wait_for` on a ref action or
  `press`, or `computer_wait` with `text`, `element`, `menu` or
  `window`. A `wait_for` selector is `role:text` in agent-desktop's role
  names (a macOS toggle is `switch`); until a snapshot has shown you the
  role, wait on the text alone (`:Saved`) and pass `wait_timeout` (e.g.
  `5000`), since a selector that never matches holds the call for 30 s.
- **The app sets** the session and your cursor: never pass `--session`,
  `--agent-id` or `--trace`.
- **`--headed`** (physical input) is allowed or refused for every agent by
  the user's settings; when it is refused, tell the user if the task needs it.
  That setting is the user's permission the guide asks for. Allowed is not a
  default: it moves the user's pointer, takes their focus and is slower. Use
  it where only physical input works: double-click, triple-click, `hover`,
  `drag`, the mouse commands, controls the accessibility tree does not
  expose, and once to retry a headless write whose own result shows no change
  (common in web pages) or a visible control whose ref action ended in
  `actionability_timeout`. Here that overrides the guide's "never switch to
  headed mode to recover". `press` sends real key events to `app` without
  `headed`; on `press`, `headed` only brings the window forward first
  (which can end an edit in progress, such as a Finder rename), and
  `press` with `headed` and no `app` types into the frontmost window.
- **Refused:** paths on the user's computer (`screenshot`'s output path,
  `clipboard-get --out`, `clipboard-set --image` / `--file-url`,
  `--screenshot`), `launch --cdp` / `--arg` / `--env` / `--cwd`,
  `press --force`, and the commands `session`, `trace` and
  `cursor-overlay`.
- **Approval.** The user approves each app before you act in it, so a first
  call in an app may wait. A denial stands: do not retry it.
- **Opening a web address** in a browser: send `press` `cmd+l` (or `cmd+t`
  for a new tab; `ctrl+l` / `ctrl+t` on Windows, where `cmd` is the
  Windows key) with the browser as `app`, together with a `snapshot` of
  the browser with `interactive_only`, and take the address field's ref from
  that snapshot (Safari: a textfield "smart search field"; the ref stays
  valid across tabs and page loads). `set_value` the URL on it, then
  `press` `return` with `wait_for` set to text on the new page. A
  `set_value` on an address bar that does not have focus reports success but
  does not navigate.
- **File panels** (Open, Save, Export): the name field takes a file name
  only; a path typed there becomes part of the name. Choose the folder with
  the Where popup or the sidebar. If the popup's ref action ends in
  `actionability_timeout`, `get` its `bounds`, `mouse_click` its centre
  with `headed`, and pick the folder from a `snapshot` with `surface`
  `menu`. If the panel's refs come back `STALE_REF` straight from a fresh
  snapshot, `mouse_click` the field with `headed` at its point (a
  `snapshot` with `include_bounds`), then send keys with `press`,
  `headed` and no `app`: with `app`, keys go to that app's process, which
  a panel drawn by another process does not receive. After saving, the
  window's title should be the bare file name.
- **Sign-in prompts:** describe what they ask for so the user can be asked;
  never ask for a password in chat. **Consequential actions** (sending,
  submitting, purchases, deleting, changing settings): do what the task
  asked for and nothing beyond it. A change the user asked for, in System
  Settings too, is authorized by that request; access to an app does not
  authorize everything else in it.

# agent-desktop

agent-desktop is a CLI that lets an AI agent observe and operate desktop apps through the OS accessibility tree. It is a tool, not an agent. Every command prints one JSON envelope (`ok`, `data` or `error`). The observe, act and verify loop runs in you.

## The loop

Use `find` when you know the role or exact name. Otherwise map the app first and drill into one region.

```
agent-desktop snapshot --skeleton --app "Notes" -i --compact   # shallow map, children_count on cut branches
agent-desktop snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact        # drill into one region
agent-desktop click @s8f3k2p9:e12                              # act on a qualified ref
agent-desktop snapshot --root @s8f3k2p9:e3 -i --compact        # verify: re-read the same region
```

- A small app needs no skeleton. Take a full `snapshot -i`.
- `-i` keeps interactive nodes only, so a row's static-text label is dropped. To tell which row a repeated button belongs to, drill that row's container with `--root` and leave out `-i`. On Windows and Linux that reads the row but does not make its button actionable: a button repeated in other rows is a twin in the window and its ref is refused (see Refs).
- A `--root` drill adds its refs to the same snapshot id. Refs outside the drilled subtree, and the drilled root itself, stay valid; refs that were already inside it are replaced, so an old ref there returns `STALE_REF`.
- Never skeleton a surface (`--surface menu`, `sheet`, `alert`). A surface is already focused.
- An action that opens a menu, sheet or alert lists it in `data.surfaces`. Target that overlay next.
- After an async step, use `wait` (see `/opt/gamut/docs/computer-use/commands-system.md`). A fixed sleep is a race.

## Refs

- Output refs are qualified: `@<snapshot_id>:e<N>`, for example `@s8f3k2p9:e1`. Pass them to later commands as they are.
- Refs are valid for one snapshot. After any UI change, re-drill the affected region or take a new snapshot.
- Only addressable elements get refs. Static text and inert containers do not.
- A command re-identifies the element before it acts. On macOS the ref carries the element's own address, so identical twins each keep their ref. On Windows and Linux a ref resolves only when it was the only element in the window its snapshot captured with its role, native id, name and description, counted even below a skeleton or depth cut, and exactly one live element still matches. Identical twins there have no ref path: only `--headed mouse-click --xy X,Y` can choose one, it takes the foreground, and a Linux Wayland session refuses it.
- `STALE_REF`: the element is gone or no longer matches. `details.kind` is `saved_ref_absent`, or `retained_object_stale` on macOS. Take a fresh snapshot and use the new ref.
- `AMBIGUOUS_TARGET`: an identical element appeared (`saved_ref_ambiguous`), or the ref was not proven unique at capture (`identity_not_unique`). Repeating the ref or re-snapshotting identical twins gives the same refusal; act on a control that is unique in the window. `identity_not_unique` also follows a snapshot that could not read the whole window in time: retake it with a larger `--timeout-ms`.
- `TIMEOUT` with `details.kind: resolution_identity_unknown`: a live read did not answer, so identity is unproven. Nothing was sent; retry.
- `SNAPSHOT_NOT_FOUND`: the snapshot id expired. Snapshot again.

## Delivery and retry

Action results carry `data.disposition` and errors carry `error.disposition`, each with `delivery` and `retry`. Observation commands such as `snapshot` have none on success; their errors, and every `INVALID_ARGS` refusal, carry `not_delivered` and `retry: safe`.

- Retry or substitute an action only when `disposition.retry` is `safe`. Only `not_delivered` is safe.
- Any other delivery value means the action may have landed. A repeat can click, type or submit twice, and `toggle` can undo itself.
- On a result that is not safe, read the live state (`get`, `is`, or a fresh snapshot) and decide from that. `details.post_state` helps when present.
- Branch on `error.code` and `error.disposition`. Message and suggestion text can change.
- `details.retryable: false` means waiting cannot change the outcome. Try a different approach.

## Headless and headed

Ref actions are headless by default. They use semantic accessibility calls and do not take focus, move the cursor, synthesize keys or use the clipboard. If no semantic path exists, the action fails closed. Use the global `--headed` flag only when the user explicitly permits physical input, such as double-click, hover, drag, or focus. Never switch to headed mode to recover from a headless failure. Raw coordinates (`--xy`) never imply focus. Which actions need `--headed` differs by OS: read the platform skill.

## References

Load one only when you need it: `/opt/gamut/docs/computer-use/<reference>.md`.

| Reference | Open it when |
|-----------|--------------|
| `commands-observation` | You need `snapshot`, `find`, `get`, `is`, `screenshot`, `list-surfaces` semantics, partial trees, or the `--root` rules |
| `commands-interaction` | You choose between click, type, set-value, select, toggle, scroll, press and mouse commands, or you debug an action error |
| `commands-system` | You launch or close apps, manage windows, use the clipboard, `wait`, `batch`, sessions, multi-agent cursors, tracing, or load skills |
| `workflows` | You want worked patterns (forms, menus, dialogs, waiting for a new window, scroll-find, drag) and the anti-patterns list |
